speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you describe exactly when these symptoms started and if they are constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury from being caught in the jersey. Did you notice any immediate deformity or a "popping" sensation at the moment of impact, and is the swelling now affecting the entire finger or just the middle segment?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion fracture of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon at the distal phalanx).

The specific finding of an inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger, combined with the mechanism of injury where the finger was forcibly extended while the tip was held in flexion, confirms a tear of the FDP tendon. I recommend obtaining a wrist and hand X-ray to rule out an associated avulsion fracture of the distal phalanx before proceeding to surgical consultation.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
